correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge4\) the presentation gives a unique normal form \(r^i s^\epsilon\). All possible generator-image pairs are exhausted by \(x\in\langle r\rangle\), \(y\) central (four maps), \(x\in\langle r\rangle\), \(y\) an outside involution (\(m^2/2\) maps), and \(x\) outside \(\langle r\rangle\) (\(2m\) maps). The parity obstruction excludes all outside \(x\) of order four. Direct valuations give each dihedral image order, and images of order four are Klein four. Idempotence leaves exactly \(m\) projections onto \(C_2\) and two trivial/full cases. Automorphism transitivity splits those \(m\) projections into two orbits of size \(m/2\). The geometric mass and tail arguments prove total-variation convergence. The included standard-library checker exhaustively tests \(n=4,5,6,7\) with direct image, multiplication and conjugacy enumeration; it is corroboration only.

originality.rationale: Full semidihedral family endomorphism image-order and isomorphism-type polynomial, explicit kernel-sensitive retraction orbit decomposition, and geometric index distribution are not stated or implied by the verified source statements inspected. The 2023 p-group classification concerns Hughes/tidy structure and semidihedral presentations, while the earlier endomorphism semigroup theorems concern recognition, and the 1996 results impose coprime cyclic factors. Puusemp 2002 is a material full-text access risk, not silently classified as noncovering. Neighboring dihedral/quaternion results do not imply the semidihedral-specific multiplicities. See four checks and source inspections below.
residual_risks: The full text of Puusemp (2002), a prime-power cyclic-semiproduct paper directly within the group family, was inaccessible. It could contain an implicit or explicit stronger generator-image classification, creating unresolved historical-priority risk.
The 2005 order-16 characterization was available only at abstract level; the smallest finite instance could be a previously tabulated special case.
A broader unindexed endomorphism-monoid classification could subsume the explicit polynomial or its consequences. No uniqueness of publication priority is asserted.

value.rationale: The complete image-order-and-type spectrum, all retraction image types, and full automorphism-orbit classification are natural structural invariants across an infinite \(2\)-group family; they are motivated by the known cyclic-index-two maximal-class trichotomy and recent tidy-group classification. The proper-nonabelian-dihedral quotient spectrum coexists with the absence of proper nontrivial retractions of order above two, and the geometric index law quantifies a substantial asymptotic phenomenon. This is not a relabeling or an isolated small-dimension numerical computation; it characterizes all orders \(2^n\) and explains the distribution of nonabelian quotient indices.
